result.response:
I have resolved the issue where `Model.objects.all().delete()` was generating unnecessary `WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM ...)` subqueries instead of a direct `DELETE FROM table`.

### Cause of the Issue
In `SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`, the calculation `sum(self.query.alias_refcount[t] > 0 for t in self.query.alias_map) == 1` was performed before the initial table alias was populated on un-compiled querysets (such as `Model.objects.all()`). When `self.query.alias_map` was empty (`{}`), `sum(...)` evaluated to `0`, causing `single_alias` to return `False`. As a result, `SQLDeleteCompiler.as_sql()` fell back to generating a subquery `WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM ...)`.

### Solution
Updated `SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias` in [`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1407-L1412) to ensure `self.query.get_initial_alias()` is called when `self.query.alias_map` has not been initialized yet, consistent with `SQLCompiler.setup_query()`. Added a unit test in [`tests/delete/tests.py`](file:///testbed/tests/delete/tests.py#L707-L711).
